title: Xeniolum prudentia, pietate, eruditione ... a Johanne noetio juniore (1586)
shelf_note: A printed neo-Latin occasional poem (a New Year's 'xeniolum' to a town senator, retelling Creation, Fall and Nativity). No tradition or collection assigned; it is a devotional/humanist gift poem, not obviously within the library's esoteric/early-science core.
structure_note: pages_count 30, pages_ocr 27, pages_translated 11: most OCR'd pages are untranslated. Page 6 carries signature 'A 4' and page 7 'A 3', yet page 6's catchword 'Jamq;' opens page 7, so the text runs on correctly; the signature order points to a misbound or misprinted signature, not a scan error. Page 10 is a blank verso (only mirrored show-through) that has been OCR'd and translated as if it held text.

title: Cabbalistic Texts: Christoph Froschmayr von Scheibenhof (PH239)
shelf_note: An 18th-century Latin manuscript of Christian-kabbalistic alchemy (Tiphereth/Geburah, gematria, Sulphur Martis, Matred/Mehetabel) from the BPH: squarely within the library's core.
structure_note: Pages 169 OCR'd and 154 translated out of 172. The manuscript's page numbers run 37 (seq 45) → 76 (seq 84), one page per image, but then 76 → 174 (seq 122): 98 written pages over 38 images. That points to a gap in the scan or a jump in the scribe's numbering. It is worth checking, but these three pages cannot settle it.

book_verdict: A good read of a hard 18th-century hand, with the Hebrew mostly right. The weak points are the alchemical signs (Sulphur Martis loses 'Martis'; ☿ is labelled sulphur) and one normalisation of 'Mai Sahab' to 'Mehetabel'; nothing a reader would be gravely misled by. The printed page numbers jump between seq 84 and 122, which should be checked.

structure_note: 520 pages, all OCR'd, 512 translated; the three pages read are in order (Liber VII medicine, XIIII geography, XVII plants). Nothing odd in the counts.
